lines.text: Every orbit begins with a door.
Open it, and the ground lets go.
Then the world rises to meet you. Blue, and impossibly thin at the edge.
Ninety minutes to circle it. Sixteen sunrises in a single day.
On the night side, cities glow like embers. Every light is someone, still awake.
And once in a long while, the moon steps in front of the sun.
The day goes out, and the sun shows what it hides: its crown.
Then the light comes back. It always does.
